title: git-vouch-migrate: continuity hardening
description: Settled by Claude on implementer recommendation, for Mark's review (round 3): (1) auth-subkey continuity requires that subkey to have actually signed the person-file version (listing a copyable public key is not proof); (2) a continuity proof is judged against the person-file version it was made for, found in git history (METARULE 1), so later add-key/retire-key/email edits do not silently drop the holder from draft runs; (3) the late cutoff is enforced by verify-continuity and drafts via --cutoff DATE, comparing the date the proof's commit landed on the registry's main branch; (4) drafts include certifications that had expired by C (same reasoning as SHA-1: the draft is a reminder); (5) drafts --as needs no continuity proof from the certifier (migratedFrom suffices; the draft is signed with the certifier's own SSH key); certifications made with a certifier's other GPG keys are not read for the flag day; (6) a holder sharing an email with another key under a different name may still prove continuity (drafts only repeat certified UIDs).
acceptance_criteria: Tests with throwaway GPG keys and real git history for each item; runbook updated for --cutoff.
notes: WITHDRAWN item (3) (Mark 2026-10-22, vouch-omzm.8): the late cutoff is policy only. No --cutoff in verify-continuity or drafts; registry maintainers merge no change adding/altering migratedFrom or adding people/*.json.asc after the cutoff (DESIGN.md flag day step 4). Items (1),(2),(4),(5),(6) stand.
